change: Coordinate native <=8-token rows using whole-request cohorts of at most48 unique experts. Each cohort borrows common immutable expert handles once; every request retains original decode arithmetic, routing order and scratch. All consumers drain before lease release.

architecture.ownership: Request-local activations, decode tables, counters and scratch remain private. Model anatomy/quant semantics and GPU backend APIs/kernels unchanged. Mutable group metadata stays in transformer-owned request state.
architecture.bounds: Union<=BN_GPU_DECODE_EXL3_MAX_EXPERTS=48, the existing singleton maximum. Fixed call-stack metadata and four sizeof-quoted group counters. Additional live or lazily populated temporary expert bundles use existing slots and may remain in the existing idle pool, bounded by its prior quota; no new activation/staging/cache quota.
architecture.lifetime: Partial acquisition, BUSY and queued failure drain all consumers and release acquired leases. Existing full-forward publication/cancellation rules retained. Mixed small/large cohorts use existing fallback.
architecture.arithmetic: Original source-order active lists, raw router IDs/weights, 8*topk scratch geometry, per-request kernels and shared-dense FFN retained. No partial-row reduction or expert concatenation.

counters.interpretation: private_kernel_submissions counts successful per-consumer trellis_decode_resident API submissions; each submission executes the existing multi-kernel decoder, so this is not an actual CUDA kernel count. Decode kernels remain per request. Reused bindings count multiple consumers of one immutable lease in a completed cohort; they do not count avoided GPU kernels or prove H2D savings on an already-cached path.

correctness.criteria: Exact full F32 vocabulary bytes and input IDs against independently captured immutable values, plus greedy IDs, streamed UTF8 and positions. Four domains/revisits, original2050/1026 histories,20requests/16live; both admissions; normal/sanitized.

performance.selection: The original admitted-cache series is rejected for nonzero filesystem input. A new prospectively fixed complete three-pair holdout uses identical order and gates. Other profiles retain the original full three-pair results. Selection is based on I/O validity, never the measured speed ratio.

protocol.scope: Bounded shared expert leases for native <=8-token decode cohorts; original per-request kernel arithmetic and scratch layouts retained.
invariants: Every source row keeps its original active-expert order, raw router IDs/weights, 8*topk scratch geometry and private decode kernel; no row concatenation, split-K change or partial expert reduction.
Greedy whole-request cohorts have at most48 unique experts, the existing singleton bound. No new GPU cache, staging, activation or persistent model state. Bounded host stack metadata only.

All consumers drain before any cohort lease is released. BUSY releases acquired prefixes before returning; hard errors discard through existing group ownership; session history/logits publish only at full success.
Mixed <=8/>8 rows retain existing fallback; the model/quant/backend APIs and routing/admission semantics remain unchanged.
New counters separately report coordinated decode layers, lease cohorts, private kernel submissions and reused expert bindings; they do not imply joint decode GPU kernels.

performance.acceptance: Output exact; any claimed decode speed gain must exceed5% GM and warm whole-burst latency no worse than1.05; otherwise declare no speed gain. Transfer saving requires actual byte accounting, not borrow counters. Filesystem state disclosed and input blocks recorded.
performance.filesystem_gate: All timed targets must report wait4 input_blocks=0; otherwise preserve the attempt and mark the timing comparison confounded.

limitations: Declared adapted DeepSeek INT4/F16 native CUDA profile; no original full-runtime equivalence or universal workload claim.
High-concurrency workload repeats four distinct histories.16live correctness does not by itself prove performance for16 unseen histories.
